heroHeadline: Niger Mutiny Contained at Niamey's Base 101 — Russia Confirms Africa Corps Fought to Suppress It; Bamako Blockade Grinds On, Day 127
heroSubtitle: Soldiers mutinied against Gen. Abdourahamane Tchiani's junta at Niamey's Base 101 overnight August 28-29, 2026, opening fire on Diori Hamani International Airport, the presidential palace perimeter, and state broadcaster ORTN headquarters — the first internal military challenge to the junta since its July 2023 coup. Niger's Defence Ministry said the mutiny was contained within roughly 24 hours; on August 30, Russia's ambassador Viktor Voropaev confirmed to TASS that 200-300 Africa Corps personnel stationed at Base 101 gave direct ground and aerial support to loyalist forces, the first known instance of Russian troops in Niger fighting to suppress an internal challenge rather than conducting counterinsurgency (Algeria also sent air support). State media's 'dozens' killed-or-arrested figure is unverified by Reuters/AP; Niger's government calls it a contained disciplinary incident, while BBC and France 24 describe an attempted coup. ACTIVE FRONTS: (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE: JNIM's fuel and supply interdiction around the capital, declared a 'total siege' April 28, remains a structural chokehold — 300+ fuel tankers destroyed and 1,000+ convoys escorted since inception, with JNIM's Aug 9 assault on FAMa's San barracks (Ségou Region, 10+ soldiers killed) showing continued southward reach. (2) MALI-NIGER PRISONER DIPLOMACY: the FLA freed a third batch of 60+ Malian soldiers at the Niger border on Aug 28, its third such release this month. (3) FLA-JNIM ALLIANCE: an ISS analysis (Sept 2) assesses the Kidal-region coalition as militarily active but fragile, split between the FLA's secular Azawad independence goal and JNIM's Islamist aims. (4) HUMANITARIAN: the Sahel recorded 9,928 militant-Islamist-violence deaths in the 12 months to mid-2026 (Africa Center) — 42% of Africa's continental total, with JNIM responsible for roughly 76% of regional deaths.
